pipeline: PaperBanana Planner -> deterministic SVG render -> PaperBanana Critic
critic_suggestions:
The overall six-panel narrative and all four MAE values are present, but the rendering needs several content and presentation corrections.

1. Panel A uses glossy 3D ball-and-stick imagery with oversized atom spheres, contrary to the requested restrained planar chemical depiction. The gas-phase and hydrated solute representations also switch visual conventions, weakening identity continuity. Use the same chemically plausible 2D solute in both states. Consolidate the separated “transfer,” “gas,” and “water” labels into one clear arrow labeled “gas → water.” The required amber bridge to panel B, labeled “compute or measure once in external data,” is missing.

2. The intended braided, continuous A→B→C→D→E narrative is not visually realized. Panels currently read mainly as isolated rows. Add explicit, noncrossing inter-panel connectors: A→B for reusable external supervision, B→C for distillation, C→D for the predicted response vector, D→E for frozen deployment, and E→F for matched evaluation.

3. Panel B contains six correct source families and correctly combines OpenFF and GBn2 into two coordinates, but the tributary routing is crowded and ambiguous. The lines overlap behind the cards and resemble a common quantitative band. Replace them with clean individual amber tributaries entering a single pale-teal conceptual response field. OpenFF and GBn2 should first meet at one compact capsule labeled exactly “2 corrected response coordinates.” The ConfSolv subtitle is visibly clipped/overprinted and must read “conformer reweighting + water-response summaries.” Use exact singular/plural badges: “1 coordinate,” “5 coordinates,” and “6 coordinates.” Add the outgoing label “distil heterogeneous response signals.”

4. Panel C abbreviates the model families as “QM,” “Abr,” “SMD,” and “Conf,” making correspondence with panel B less explicit. Either use full family names or provide compact unambiguous labels. The 15-channel grouping is difficult to verify because labels collide beneath the bars; render visibly countable groups as 1 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 6 with separators, braces, and full source labels. Keep all channels within a teal family rather than using amber for the first coordinate, since amber denotes external sources while teal denotes learned coordinates. The benchmark exclusion is only a dashed underline; show benchmark-equivalent molecules outside a dashed teacher-training enclosure with an explicit gray exclusion mark. Use the exact note “benchmark-equivalent molecules excluded from supervised response teachers.”

5. Panel D lacks the required small molecular-structure origin for the Morgan fingerprint and RDKit descriptors, so the ordinary structure-feature path appears disconnected. Add a navy molecule labeled “ordinary structure features,” branching to both feature representations. Add a vertical dotted boundary between Stage 1 and Stage 2 and the note “separate training stages.” The endpoint supervision label should read exactly “supervised by experimental hydration free energies,” with its arrow terminating only at the endpoint ensemble. The bottom PIMD note is crowded by a rule/connector and appears malformed; reset it cleanly as “No PIMD-derived feature in the final stack.” Keep magenta absent from this panel.

6. Panel E communicates simulation-free deployment well, but the lower feature arrow visually collides with text and the endpoint block. Redraw the route as two clean inputs—response vector and structure features—merging only at the frozen endpoint ensemble. Add “predicted hydration free energy” beneath ΔGhyd. Use the exact vector grouping 1 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 6 and ensure the same coordinate order as panel C. The example SMILES CC(N)=O is chemically valid, but the molecular graph should use the same planar style as the rest of the figure. Do not include water or physical-calculation imagery in this panel.

7. Panel F preserves the exact values and honestly uses a common scale. However, the requested comparison annotations are reduced to small prose above the plot. Add a visible bracket from 0.303 to 0.202 labeled “response priors reduce matched MAE,” and a subtle brace pairing 0.303 with 0.306 labeled “shuffling abolishes the gain.” Separate the magenta ARROW/PIMD8 row more clearly with whitespace or a divider, and place “accuracy reference; not a teacher” and “never used as a SolvAI input” directly beside that row. Do not imply statistical superiority of 0.202 over 0.205.

8. Several labels are too small, crowded, or partially overlapped, especially in B, C, D, and F. Increase minimum text size, shorten local copy where possible, and reserve more whitespace around connectors. Maintain consistent 1.5–2 pt strokes and one arrowhead per directional relationship.

9. The caption itself is correctly excluded from the image and should remain separate. No text-based color legend should be added.
revised_description:
Retain the original six-panel, three-row landscape composition, white or warm off-white background, large bold A–F panel letters, abundant whitespace, and semantic palette. Improve it by establishing a clearly traceable, noncrossing A→B→C→D→E flow plus a thin E→F evaluation link. Use deep navy for molecular structure and ordinary molecular features, amber for external physical or empirical sources, teal for learned response coordinates and inference, neutral gray for repeated or excluded computation, and magenta only for the ARROW/PIMD8 reference in F. Use flat planar chemistry, horizontal sans-serif text, 1.5–2 pt connectors, and exactly one arrowhead per directional relationship. Do not include a caption, color legend, gradients, shadows, glossy 3D atoms, or decorative circuitry.

Panel A — repeated-computation bottleneck: Replace the glossy ball-and-stick render with the same modest, chemically plausible 2D neutral solute on both sides. Place one copy in a sparse gas region and one in a small water environment. Connect them with one horizontal arrow labeled “gas → water.” Show three muted gray trajectory frames with changing water arrangements, a restrained clock/sampling-ring symbol, and a small stack of repeated solute silhouettes. Include “new solute,” “repeat sampling / free-energy calculation,” and “accurate, but costly per molecule.” From the physical-response side, draw an amber arrow into B labeled “compute or measure once in external data,” making clear that these data are reusable supervision rather than deployment-time simulation.

Panel B — complementary response teachers: Preserve six unequal source cards, but space them around one pale-teal softly rounded conceptual field labeled “complementary solvent-response information.” Avoid a shared axis or tangled background bands. Each card sends one clean amber tributary toward the field. Use: “CombiSolv-QM / COSMOtherm,” subtitle “water response,” badge “1 coordinate”; “Abraham empirical axes,” with five ticks, badge “5 coordinates”; “OpenFF explicit-water response,” subtitle “residual-corrected”; “GBn2 implicit-water response,” subtitle “residual-corrected”; “MolSolv SMD(water),” badge “1 coordinate”; and “ConfSolv,” subtitle “conformer reweighting + water-response summaries,” badge “6 coordinates.” Ensure no text is clipped. OpenFF and GBn2 must first converge into one compact amber capsule labeled “2 corrected response coordinates,” after which one tributary enters the conceptual field. Beneath the field, retain the note “heterogeneous scales and approximations · no shared fidelity axis.” A single teal-forward connector labeled “distil heterogeneous response signals” exits toward C.

Panel C — distillation into reusable coordinates: At left, show several varied planar navy molecular structures labeled “molecular structure.” Feed them with thin navy arrows into six plain rounded surrogate modules grouped under “independent structure → response surrogates.” Use compact but unambiguous family labels: “CombiSolv-QM / COSMOtherm,” “Abraham,” “OpenFF,” “GBn2,” “MolSolv SMD(water),” and “ConfSolv.” Do not use brain or generic AI icons. Teal output arrows converge into exactly 15 narrow, countable teal channels. Divide the channels with visible gaps and braces into 1 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 6 and label the groups “CombiSolv-QM / COSMOtherm: 1,” “Abraham: 5,” “OpenFF + GBn2 corrected responses: 2,” “MolSolv SMD(water): 1,” and “ConfSolv: 6.” Place one brace over the complete vector reading “15 predicted, molecule-aligned response coordinates.” Add “predicted from structure; not recomputed for each query.” Show teacher-training molecules within a light dashed boundary and a pale-gray benchmark-equivalent set outside it with a clear gray exclusion mark. Label this boundary note exactly “benchmark-equivalent molecules excluded from supervised response teachers.” The exclusion mark must not cross the predicted vector.

Panel D — experimentally supervised endpoint: Continue the 15-channel teal vector directly from C and label it “predicted 15-response vector.” Add a small navy molecular structure icon labeled “ordinary structure features.” Branch it into a binary-cell strip labeled “2,048-bit Morgan fingerprint” and an ordered line stack labeled “217 RDKit 2D descriptors.” Route the vector, fingerprint, and descriptors through three distinct noncrossing arrows that meet only at three restrained overlapping rounded blocks labeled “endpoint ensemble.” Beneath the ensemble, place a small measurement-table/data-point symbol labeled “supervised by experimental hydration free energies,” with one upward arrow terminating only at the ensemble. From the ensemble, draw one teal arrow to “ΔGhyd.” Insert a thin vertical dotted divider between C and D. Label the left side “Stage 1: structure → response,” the right side “Stage 2: responses + structure → endpoint,” and below the divider “separate training stages.” Along the bottom, place the unobstructed gray note “No PIMD-derived feature in the final stack.” Do not use magenta or connect ARROW/PIMD8 to this panel.

Panel E — simulation-free deployment: Keep E as the largest focal panel on a very pale teal field. Build one clean left-to-right inference path. At left, use a compact card labeled “new SMILES,” containing the valid monospaced example “CC(N)=O.” A navy arrow leads to a matching planar molecular graph. From that graph, one arrow enters a block labeled “frozen structure → response models,” with a small lock or snowflake only as a secondary cue. Its output is the same compact 15-channel teal vector, visibly grouped 1 | 5 | 2 | 1 | 6. A separate short branch from the molecular graph produces a fingerprint strip and descriptor stack labeled “Morgan fingerprint + RDKit descriptors.” Route exactly two clean arrows—the response vector and ordinary structure features—into a block labeled “frozen endpoint ensemble.” Avoid crossing arrows or running connectors through text. A bold teal arrow leads to the large output “ΔGhyd,” with “predicted hydration free energy” directly beneath it. Above the frozen blocks, place “learned response information is reused.” Center below the pipeline: “No MD · No PIMD · No probe calculation.” Do not depict water, trajectories, continuum cavities, alchemical paths, or probe calculations in E.

Panel F — matched evidence: Connect E to F only with a thin neutral evaluation arrow labeled “matched evaluation.” Use a compact horizontal lollipop or bar chart on a common linear 0.00–0.35 axis labeled “MAE (kcal mol⁻¹) — lower is better,” with sparse pale-gray grid lines. Above it, place “Matched 85-solute ARROW chemistry” and the restrained headline “PIMD8-level accuracy on this reference chemistry.” Plot and directly label exactly: “Matched structure-only — 0.303” in medium gray/navy; “SolvAI — 0.202” in saturated teal; “Shuffled response priors — 0.306” in light gray with a small shuffle cue; and “ARROW/PIMD8 — 0.205” in magenta. Give the magenta row extra whitespace or a thin divider from the learned-model rows. Beside it place “accuracy reference; not a teacher” and “never used as a SolvAI input.” Add a thin difference bracket from structure-only 0.303 to SolvAI 0.202 labeled “response priors reduce matched MAE.” Pair structure-only 0.303 and shuffled priors 0.306 with a subtle gray brace labeled “shuffling abolishes the gain.” Keep SolvAI and PIMD8 nearly equal in encoded length and add no stars, victory marks, or statistical-superiority claim. Magenta must remain entirely within F with no continuation into any training or deployment panel.
